title: Sell Mineral Rights in Cadiz, OH
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Cadiz, OH | Harrison County Seat
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Cadiz, the Harrison County seat, in the Utica core? Learn where records are kept and get a straightforward cash offer.
heroLead: Cadiz is the Harrison County seat, which makes it the record-keeping center for a county sitting in the thickest part of Ohio's Utica play.
intro: Every deed, lease, division order assignment, and dormant mineral notice affecting mineral rights anywhere in Harrison County eventually runs through the recorder's office right here in Cadiz. If you own minerals in or around town, or anywhere else in the county for that matter, this courthouse is where the paper trail lives.

Harrison County has some of the thickest, most productive Utica/Point Pleasant rock in Ohio, and Cadiz-area acreage has been leased and developed since the play's earliest days, which means most tracts here carry a decade or more of documented history by now.

sections.heading: Working directly from the county seat
paragraphs: Because you're close to the recorder's office, a title search or record pull on your Cadiz-area tract is often more straightforward than it would be for owners working from out of state trying to research a distant county remotely. If you're not sure exactly what your family owns, an in-person or online records check here is the fastest way to get real answers.
The same office also maintains the index for any dormant mineral abandonment notices, which is worth checking if your family's interest has sat quiet for a long stretch.

sections.heading: Development density around Cadiz
paragraphs: Multi-well pads and long horizontal laterals are common throughout the townships surrounding Cadiz, and the county has drawn sustained operator interest since 2011. If your tract is inside an active spacing unit, your division order and royalty statements are the clearest measure of current value.

sections.heading: What to bring if you're selling
paragraphs: Your deed, any lease documents, and recent royalty statements if the tract is producing are the core pieces of paperwork worth gathering. If you've inherited the interest and don't have a deed in your own name yet, the estate document, will, or affidavit of heirship that establishes your ownership is the starting point instead.

faqs.question: Where exactly do I go to research my Cadiz-area mineral title?
faqs.answer: The Harrison County Recorder's office, located in Cadiz, holds the full deed and lease record for the county and is the starting point for any title search.

faqs.question: Is Cadiz in the strongest part of the Utica play?
faqs.answer: Yes, Harrison County sits in the core of the play, and the area around Cadiz has seen sustained development since the earliest permits were issued.

faqs.question: I inherited my interest but never transferred the deed into my name. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: It's common and fixable, usually through recording the will or an affidavit of heirship establishing your ownership before a sale closes.
